entities.name: Gentamicin
observations: Short-course prophylactic gentamicin in open-fracture cohorts was not associated with an excess AKI signal in available comparative retrospective studies.
AKI risk among exposed trauma patients was associated with hypotension, higher injury severity, ICU admission, contrast exposure, age, and weight; causality from gentamicin was not established.

entities.name: Acute kidney injury
observations: In open-fracture prophylaxis cohorts, AKI was approximately 4% with cefazolin plus gentamicin versus 4.8% with cefazolin alone in one RIFLE-based retrospective study.
Another cohort found no association between prophylactic gentamicin and AKI: OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.020–2.44, p=0.22; admission hypotension and injury severity were associated with AKI.
A Gustilo IIIA cohort reported one AKI case in a pooled amikacin/gentamicin group and one in the ampicillin/sulbactam group.

entities.name: Open fractures
observations: Evidence on gentamicin prophylaxis and AKI consists predominantly of small retrospective cohorts and chart-review series; no direct systematic review pooling this association was identified.
Gentamicin dose, duration, and AKI timing were incompletely reported, and trauma-related confounding limits causal inference.
